generations.name: First generation
generations.note: Launched Toyota's mass-market era in Japan, then the world. Light, simple, rear-wheel drive.

generations.name: Fourth generation
generations.note: The last rear-drive Corolla line — its AE86 coupe variant became the most famous drift car ever built.

generations.name: Twelfth generation
generations.note: Sharper styling, hybrid everywhere, and the GR Corolla hot hatch with a turbo three-cylinder and all-wheel drive.

models.intro: The best-selling nameplate in history — more than 50 million sold. The Corolla is the default answer to 'what car should I buy?' on every continent, and the GR Corolla proves the badge can still have a pulse.
models.name: Corolla

generations.name: Third generation
generations.note: The rounded 'wide-body' Camry that set the 1990s quality benchmark Detroit spent a decade chasing.

generations.name: Eighth generation
generations.note: First Camry with genuine styling intent and a chassis tuned to be driven, not just operated.

generations.name: Ninth generation
generations.note: Hybrid-only powertrain lineup, standard safety tech, optional all-wheel drive.

models.intro: America's best-selling sedan for over two decades. The Camry is the car as appliance done perfectly — and since 2024, hybrid-only, which tells you where the whole segment went.
models.name: Camry

models.collectorNote: A80 prices detached from reality years ago — clean six-speed turbos are six-figure cars. Buy the best-documented car, not the cheapest.

generations.name: Third generation (Mk III)
generations.note: First Supra fully divorced from the Celica line. Turbo models made 232 hp when that was serious speed.

generations.name: Fourth generation (Mk IV)
generations.note: The icon. Sequential twin turbos, a Getrag six-speed, and an iron-block engine that tuners have pushed past 1,000 hp for thirty years.

generations.name: Fifth generation (GR Supra)
generations.note: Built with BMW around the B58 inline-six. Purists argued; the stopwatch disagreed — it's the fastest Supra Toyota has ever sold.

models.intro: Four generations of inline-six grand tourer, one legend: the Mk IV's 2JZ engine became the most famous tuning platform on Earth. The name returned in 2019, co-developed with BMW.
models.name: Supra

models.collectorNote: Rust and deferred maintenance decide FJ40 values more than mileage. A restored 40 is a $60k+ conversation; a honest driver is the sweet spot.

generations.name: 40 Series
generations.note: The FJ40. Two doors, removable everything, and a silhouette so right that Toyota keeps referencing it seventy years later.

generations.name: 80 Series
generations.note: Coil springs, full-time 4WD, available factory lockers. The overlanding community's forever answer.

generations.name: 300 Series
generations.note: Twin-turbo V6 replaces the V8, on a proper ladder frame. The US-market 250 Series carries the nameplate as a smaller retro-styled sibling.

models.intro: The vehicle that goes where roads apologize. From the FJ40 to the 300 Series, the Land Cruiser is the expedition default on every continent — the car aid workers and armies trust when failure isn't an option.
models.name: Land Cruiser

generations.name: First generation
generations.note: Japan-only at first, then the world's first mass-produced hybrid sedan exported from 2000.

generations.name: Second generation
generations.note: The wedge. 55 mpg combined and a silhouette that made efficiency visible — Hollywood's red-carpet car of choice.

generations.name: Fifth generation
generations.note: A concept car that escaped. Sleek monoform styling, 196 hp, and a plug-in Prime variant with real EV range.

models.intro: The car that made 'hybrid' a word your parents knew. The second generation became a cultural symbol; the fifth became, improbably, genuinely good-looking.
models.name: Prius

generations.name: First generation
generations.note: Compact-truck sizing, bombproof 3.4L V6, and the ancestor of today's overland builds.

generations.name: Third generation
generations.note: The truck that owned the segment's sales charts for a generation, with a cult following among off-road builders.

generations.name: Fourth generation
generations.note: Turbo four-cylinder or hybrid i-FORCE MAX power, coil-spring rear on most trims, and a Trailhunter trim built for overlanding from the factory.

models.intro: The midsize truck benchmark for resale value and trail credibility. Tacomas are bought, used hard for a decade, and sold for embarrassing fractions of their original price.
models.name: Tacoma

models.collectorNote: Seven-figure cars when they trade at all — most of the 351 sit in collections. The 2020 sale of a Shelby-prepared example topped $2.5M.

generations.name: Production run
generations.note: Aluminium body, Yamaha-built twin-cam head on Toyota's M six, disc brakes at every corner — specification that embarrassed contemporary European GTs.

models.intro: Japan's first supercar. Co-developed with Yamaha, hand-built in tiny numbers — 351 cars — and proof in 1967 that Japan could build a world-class GT. A Bond film made one a convertible because Sean Connery didn't fit.
models.name: 2000GT
